summary: Proceed with no companion. This is a single-shape, config-gated rewrite stage whose kernel row (sliding_cluster_kernel) and decode_32 shape time can be read directly, with eleven untouched shapes in the same run as controls. The real risks are that the in-layer saving comes in well under the ~16 us that summing the profile's kernel times predicts, and that a warm-L2 prepare selector picks the wrong path.
justification: Plausible on H200. Master's sliding batch>1 chain is still SGLang's: FusedQKNorm, the k/v/q FP8 casts, store_cache, FA3 prepare_varlen_num_blocks 2.2 + main 23.7 + FlashAttnFwdCombine 2.8, then FusedRMSNormGate. Profile c243a29f, sliding decode_32 = 242.3 us against a floor of 84.5. The donor kernel measured 18.3 us at B=32 in muse_attention_decode (job 1990ce53e9d34073: shape 25.84 -> 20.15 us; 124 regs, 32 B spill, 103,424 B smem, MaxActiveClusters C=4 = 62, so the >= 32 gate passes). Geometry matches decode_layer (hq 16, hkv 2, d 64, qkv [T, 2304], page 1, window 2048). The KV window at B=32 is ~16.8 MB, so the floor is ~3.5 us and the kernel sits ~5x above it. Stage-1 milestone 3 (within 1.5x of the floor) is not reachable this stage, which is acceptable for a rewrite. Only sliding decode_32 is gated, so the expected flat directions on every other shape are right. WEAKEST LINK: the ~35 us incumbent figure is a sum of profile rows plus a guessed 6-8 us of 'hidden' glue, and the layer has already shown that this arithmetic overstates the realizable saving. The harvested sliding-fused-batched-decode-port replaced the same chain at decode_32 with a 22.1 us Triton kernel. That predicted about -13 us, yet the shape moved only 246.99 -> 245.52 us (delta 1.03 by paired ratio). If the same discount applies, the cluster kernel's saving is closer to -5..-10 us than -16, and the kill line 'shape not < 236' could fire even though the kernel row is below 22 us. Judge stage 1 on the kernel row against the summed incumbent rows (FA3 + combine + prepare + the casts/store/qknorm/normgate rows in the same profile), not on the 236 line alone.
confounders: full-decode-splitkv-restack-on-pdl (just landed): disjoint gate (window == 0 only), so there is no timing interaction. It does add a third load_inline module (dense chain 50 s + splitkv 49 s + cluster ~41 s = ~140 s of compile inside the 15-minute run budget), which is a timeout risk, not a confounder.

small-t-launch-minimal-dense-chain-pdl: its PDL kernels (P, R) sit after the o GEMM and attn_boundary, and the attention-side chain is plain stream order, so the cluster kernel joins no PDL edge. Note that the attention-side PDL attempt (dense-chain-stage2-attn-side-pdl) lost on sliding decode_16/32, which shows this region is sensitive to launch-order changes. A small loss could come from the cluster launch's own setup cost, not from attention.

sglang-pipeline-parity-router-hilo-m8: defines the incumbent (FusedQKNorm, FusedRMSNormGate, FA3), and the self-check compares against it. That is not a confound, but the reference chain in the self-check must be master's exact kv_scale division and q FP8 cast.

stack-align-par-sidestream-sliding1 / fa3-hdim128-head-pairing-batched / post-expert-norm-triton-small-t / marlin-block-m-cap-16: gated to batch 1, full layers, the post-expert stage or T>32 respectively. None share the replaced kernels or memory traffic at sliding decode_32, so none confound.
interference: No companion is warranted. The gate selects exactly one scored shape (sliding decode_32), and no landed hypothesis touches the kernels it replaces, so reverting one (ab-revert) would measure the same thing. The other eleven shapes are byte-identical in-run controls. The profile names sliding_cluster_kernel as its own row, so a gain, a loss or a fallback can each be read from one run: the kernel row against the summed incumbent rows, plus the PATH CHOSEN and selector-timing lines. A split control is unnecessary because the kernel is one indivisible launch. The only thing that can make a single result ambiguous is the prepare-time selector silently keeping the incumbent, and the log disambiguates that, so it needs a logging requirement, not a second run. The parallel attention re-measure (stack-streamk-ticket-cluster-c16-c4, job 195dcc1209b6457b) does not change the decision. decode_layer's incumbent at B=32 is FA3, not attention's Triton or cluster, so C=4 needs only to beat ~29+ us of FA3-plus-glue, not attention's newer master.
rules_flags: Precision: the donor kernel rounds q to E4M3 AFTER multiplying by qk_scale_factor, whereas FA3 rounds before the scale. The donor's audit judged this to be the same precision class (|q| <= ~44, normal range). P and V are f16 with fp32 softmax and accumulation, which is finer than FA3's FP8 P. This is acceptable, but keep it exactly as the donor does and do not add any coarser cast.

Do not port the donor's kernel_fn try/except RuntimeError fallback with a module-level 'noted' set as written. Under graph capture a host launch error invalidates the capture anyway. Any module state written from kernel_fn must be keyed only by config, never by data. Prefer deciding the path entirely in prepare().
Cache store: decode_layer stores with reserved_skip_index=-1 (slot 0 is a live row). The kernel must write every cache_loc, including 0, and must not skip a padding slot.
Every key: the mask must be [seq - 2047, seq] inclusive, matching window_size=(window - 1, 0). The donor's audit emulated rank coverage for C=4 at seq 0..90000; keep that partition unchanged.

kernel_fn must contain no timing, no torch.cuda.synchronize and no occupancy query. Selector timing, the canary sync and cudaOccupancyMaxActiveClusters belong in import or prepare only, as the change states.
open_questions: Prepare-time selector and L2: the B=32 KV window (~16.8 MB) fits in the H200's L2, while the judge cold-flushes L2 before every replay. A back-to-back CUDA-event comparison in prepare therefore measures both paths with warm KV and can mis-rank them. Flush L2 between selector reps (write a buffer larger than L2) or time each path as a graph after a flush, and print both numbers so the log shows whether the selector kept the incumbent.

The selector must time the incumbent as the WHOLE replaced chain (qk_norm through o_norm_gate, including the casts and store_cache) against the single cluster launch. Timing FA3 alone would bias it toward rejecting the new kernel.

None of the 13 tests has sliding at 17 <= batch <= 32, so this path is checked only on the timed decode_32 calls. A wrong result surfaces as a failed run after timing begins, not in the tests. The B in {17, 32} self-check against master's chain (rel L2 and exact cache-row equality) is the only early guard, so keep it strict.

RoPE mapping: decode_layer's sliding layers use rope_theta 500000 with interleaved RoPE via cos_sin positions. Confirm that the donor's _inv_freq/_norm_rope pairing convention matches FusedQKNorm here, as the batch-1 _sliding_fused_kernel already does in this file, and reuse that file's helpers rather than adding a second copy.

Compile budget: three load_inline modules (~140 s) plus the self-checks. Consider whether the cluster TU can share the splitkv module's build to cut one nvcc invocation; at minimum, print compile seconds per module.
If attention's job 195dcc1209b6457b re-measures C=4 at B=32 well above 18.3 us, re-read this run's kernel row with that in mind. It still does not block dispatch.
